claimed_purpose.text: Defines canonical calendar-period identities shared by every write/selection boundary

mechanisms.text: User profile is a curated text document stored in config key 'user_profile', updated incrementally each day from the day page; structured into four sections: basic info, helpful insights, recent topics, long-term preferences

Lock mechanism: memories can be permanently locked (is_permanent=true); auto/dream locks are retired (is_permanent set to false) after configurable lock_retire_days of inactivity; importance is floored at 8 on retire

Calendar system auto-compresses chat history into hierarchical summaries (day → week → month → quarter → year). Injection is Matryoshka-style: recent days get full detail, older periods get high-level overviews.

Write path for digest: LLM merges fragment texts into event entries; each entry is inserted with memory_type='daily_digest', an embedding vector, importance score, category_id, and date-prefixed content
The product exposes a /debug/memories endpoint that returns stored memory data, and an /admin interface for browsing memories, suggesting a persistent memory store with at least two read surfaces.
Tombstone rows act as a delete/forget signal; survivor buckets are rows that remain after a matching session, turn, or message tombstone, and their presence is treated as anomalous.
A period page is rejected at write time if its created_at timestamp falls on or before the period's end date, requiring explicit regeneration after the period closes
Dream background processing auto-trigger thresholds (5/7/3) are hardcoded in dream.py ~784, inconsistent with the configurable dream_drowsy_threshold (default 30)
Named memory tools (search_memory, save_memory, get_recent, lock_memory, unlock_memory) are quarantined — blocked from execution in quarantined_project scope.
A selection (retrieval) filter discards pages whose stored key is not canonical or whose period is not fully completed, enforcing read-time validity gating
A user profile field is persisted and updated via a dedicated prompt, representing a curated user model separate from raw conversation logs
After digest entries are saved, original fragment records are marked 'digested' in bulk so they no longer participate in daily injection
Memory metabolism: automatic softening of old memories is time-gated (minimum age, cooldown, daily limit)
Contradiction detection: new memory conflicting with an old one auto-invalidates the outdated version.
Memories can be auto-locked based on recall count, topic diversity, and emotional recall thresholds

ledger.claim: Memory heat decays over time and warms on recall; emotional intensity slows decay; cold memories are deleted by cleanup threshold.
ledger.quote: Every memory has a "heat" score. Time makes it naturally decay, but if you keep bringing up the same topic, it warms back up. High-emotion memories decay slower… only the cold and old get cleaned up, by heat.
ledger.label: measured

ledger.claim: Recall is defined as actual injection into the prompt, not merely retrieval from the store; injected low-resolution memories gain a 30-day heat extension.
ledger.quote: Only memories actually written into the conversation count as "recalled" — only the cold and old get cleaned up, by heat… Only memories actually injected into the prompt count as recalled; recalled low-resolution memories are extended by 30 days
ledger.locator: ### 🔥 Fades and strengthens / ### 🔥 Memory heat system (Full feature list)
ledger.label: measured

ledger.claim: Dream consolidation is a three-layer pipeline (cleanup → merge into MemScenes → foresight inference). Output MemScenes are indexed and re-injected by vector similarity in subsequent conversations.
ledger.quote: It works in three layers: first cleans up outdated and duplicate fragments, then merges related fragments into coherent "memory scenes", and finally infers things you never explicitly said but your AI should understand… consolidated scenes carry vector indexes, so when a related topic comes up during the day, they get found and flow back into the conversation.
ledger.label: measured

ledger.claim: Calendar hierarchy auto-compresses chat history into day/week/month/quarter/year summaries; injection is tiered so recent periods are detailed and older periods are summarized.
ledger.quote: The calendar system auto-compresses chat history into hierarchical summaries: day → week → month → quarter → year. When injecting into conversation, recent days get full detail, last week gets abbreviated, older periods get high-level overviews.
ledger.locator: ### 📅 Recent is vivid, distant is hazy
ledger.label: measured

ledger.claim: User-locked memories are permanent (no decay, no auto-delete). Auto-locks and Dream-promoted locks retire after 90 days without recall by demotion, not deletion.
ledger.quote: Memories you lock by hand are sacred — they never decay, never retire, never auto-delete. Machine-locked memories (auto-locks and Dream promotions) have an exit path instead: if nobody asks about them for 90 days, they get demoted from "permanent" back to high-importance regular memories (reversible, never deleted)
ledger.label: measured

ledger.claim: Project isolation is automatic; global memories, calendar, and Dream scenes are shared; each project adds a private layer that never leaks to global or other projects.
ledger.quote: global memories, calendar pages, and Dream scenes form a shared base for every chat. Each project adds a private layer of instructions, files, project memories, and project conversations. Private project content never flows into global chats or another project. No setup needed — isolation is automatic.

ledger.claim: Retrieval uses RRF hybrid search (vector + keyword in parallel, merged via Reciprocal Rank Fusion) with synonym expansion and semantic deduplication.
